title: onboarding-experiment-90-day-hypotheses-retro-jun30-2026
summary: Retro and data-backed notes from the 90-day onboarding experiment run by platform-eng. Covers hypotheses, metrics tracked, qualitative feedback from new hires and buddies, risks observed, and recommended next steps for scaling the program.
content:
Context:
We ran a targeted onboarding experiment for new engineers joining Platform Engineering between 2026-04-01 and 2026-05-15 (n=8). Goal: reduce median time-to-first-meaningful-PR and increase new-hire confidence/sense-of-belonging by testing a structured 1:1 buddy program + condensed tech onboarding path. This doc collates quantitative outcomes, qualitative feedback from check-ins, and an action-oriented risk register for the wider org.

Hypotheses tested:
- H1: A 1:1 buddy with a structured week-1 checklist reduces time-to-first-meaningful-PR by 25% vs baseline.
- H2: A shared "micro-project" (2–3 day scoped ticket) completed in week 2 increases new hire confidence and understanding of the codebase.
- H3: Weekly cohort sync + curated docs reduces number of ad-hoc Slack questions in week 1 and improves perceived onboarding clarity.

Key metrics tracked (dashboard refs: CONFL-ONB-42):
- Median time-to-first-meaningful-PR (merged): experiment = 9 days; baseline (prior 6 months) = 12 days => 25% faster (meets H1 target).
- Number of Slack 1:1 help requests (week 1 avg): experiment = 4.8 requests/new-hire; baseline = 6.2 => ~23% reduction.
- Micro-project completion rate by end of week 2: 7/8 completed (88%).
- New-hire self-reported confidence (scale 1-5) at day 14: median 4.0 vs baseline 3.2.
- Buddy time commitment logged (hrs/week): median 3.5 hrs.

Qualitative notes (synthesized from day 7/14/30 check-ins and retro):
- What worked:
  - Structured week-1 checklist (env setup, infra walkthrough, minimal runbook tasks) removed the "where to start" friction. New hires liked explicit next steps.
  - The micro-project gave a tangible ownership moment and was cited repeatedly as the first time they felt productive. It also created a straightforward PR review pattern to integrate new devs into code review culture.
  - Buddies who paired early on architecture overview reduced the follow-up meetings frequency.

- Pain points / friction observed:
  - Buddy burnout risk: buddies reported the time commitment was manageable short-term but started to encroach on scheduled work in week 4 for sustained runs. Some buddies pulled ad-hoc extra pairing to unblock hires.
  - Doc gaps: certain service-level onboarding docs (env vars, local test flakiness, common hotspots) needed updating — led to repeated questions that were not a candidate for "Slack reduction" as intended.
  - Tooling confusion: local infra shim mismatch (devcontainer vs local scripts) created inconsistent developer experience across hires and increased setup time for 2 hires.

Direct quotes (anonymized):
- "The micro-project got me involved in the repo very fast — I was able to suggest an optimization and learned the release dance."
- "My buddy was great, but in week 3 they were swamped and I had to wait on reviews — would be nice to have a backup or async checklist."

Risk register (short-term / medium-term):
- R1: Buddy capacity (medium likelihood, medium impact) — if program scales 3x, current time investment is unsustainable without formal recognition or reduced load.
  - Mitigation: formalize buddy rotation, credit buddy work in performance planning, allow 8 hours/week allocation for first month. Pilot for two sprints.
- R2: Doc debt (high likelihood, medium impact) — missing/old docs increase variance in ramp time.
  - Mitigation: triage top 10 recurring questions from experiment into a docs backlog ticket (JIRA-PLAT-1182). Create owner for each doc.
- R3: Tool parity (low likelihood, high impact) — inconsistent dev environment leads to wasted time and frustration.
  - Mitigation: standardize devcontainer with tested scripts; include smoke tests in quickstart. Add a CI check that validates devcontainer build.

Operational playbook (what we actually ran):
- Pre-start (day -7 to -1): HR + EngOps created accounts, access checklist, invited to cohort Slack channel, assigned buddy.
- Week 0/1: Buddy onboarding checklist (env setup, architecture 30-min overview, run a local smoke test, explain release cycle), 3x 30-min pairing sessions scheduled across week.
- Week 2: Micro-project assigned (sized 2–3 dev days), scheduled mid-week sync for blockers.
- Week 3–4: Gradual ramp into team backlog, buddy move to "office hours" pattern (one scheduled 1:1 + weekly office hour).

Suggested changes for next run (priority ordered):
1) Buddy recognition and bounded time: allocate a formal 8 hours/week protected for the buddy during the first 30 days and rotate buddies after 45 days. Add a quick feedback form for buddies at day 14.
2) Docs blitz: sprint to address top-10 recurring questions before next cohort; label docs with "verified-for-2026-07" once validated. Owner: Marta K. (assigned).
3) Backup reviewer pool: create "on-call" reviewer rota for micro-project PRs so new hires don't wait >48 hours for code review.
4) Dev environment parity: consolidate devcontainer + smoke test; add a CI job to validate container build on PRs that touch onboarding docs.
5) Cohort calendar: keep weekly 30-min cohort sync + 60-min monthly cross-team lunch to build social bonds.

Open questions / decisions needed from Eng Leadership:
- Q1: Do we formally compensate buddy work (credit in OKRs/velocity) or treat as unpaid cross-functional effort? Decision needed by 2026-07-14.
- Q2: Budget for docs blitz (2 engineer-weeks) — approve as part of platform sprint cycle?
- Q3: Do we adopt a standardized micro-project template across eng orgs? If yes, who owns the template?

Action items (owners & ETA):
- A1: Create JIRA epic for docs blitz + triage top-10 questions (owner: Marta Kowalski) — due 2026-07-09. -> JIRA-PLAT-1182
- A2: Draft buddy allocation policy and propose to eng leadership (owner: Aisha Patel) — due 2026-07-14.
- A3: Implement devcontainer smoke test and CI validation (owner: Noah Kim) — due 2026-07-21.
- A4: Build backup reviewer rota and list of volunteers (owner: Ethan Ruiz) — due 2026-07-07.
- A5: Run next cohort pilot (n=10) with formalized changes (owner: Priya Shah) — start 2026-08-03.

Appendix: raw signals collected (excerpt)
- Slack volume snapshot: channel #plat-onboarding : avg messages/day by cohort week: W0=18, W1=24, W2=12. Direct-mentions to buddies tracked separately.
- PR review latency: median from opened->merged for micro-projects = 30 hours. Two outliers at 96+ hours correlated with reviewer PTO.
- Buddy survey (n=6): Net promoter for program = +42; qualitative note: "Would be easier if we had a small checklist for common questions to answer in week 1."

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is purposely candid — it includes both wins and pain points. The experiment met primary ramp speed goals but surfaced operational scaling issues. Recommend approving the proposed mitigations and running the larger pilot to validate sustainability.

History / provenance:
- Experiment cohort curated from hiring funnel Q2 2026 (roles: infra engineer x3, runtime engineer x2, SRE x2, infra automation x1).
- Design doc and cohort plan: CONFL-ONB-42; onboarding issues triaged in JIRA-PLAT-1182.

Next steps: please comment inline or add to the PR for the buddy policy by 2026-07-12. If no objections, will present summary to Eng Leadership 2026-07-15.
